facts.raw_span: A woman in her 50s who was a never-smoker
presented with an enlarged, firm right ala
a lesion of the right nasal vestibule mucosa 5 years prior
biopsied and reported as a solid and cystic hidradenoma
p63 positive, pancytokeratin positive, and p16 negative
recurrence of the lesion 8 months prior to presentation
the lesion was excised but recurred quickly after 2 months
tumor within the nasal vestibule floor and ala
p63 positive and p16 negative, with positive margins
thicker right ala compared with the left ala
Downward papillomatous proliferation of small, uniform, slightly atypical keratinocytes within loose stroma
reflected ala after lateral rhinotomy showing tumor in ala and its extension into the floor of the nasal vestibule

concepts.why: The patient's initial biopsy was reported as a solid and cystic hidradenoma, and subsequent pathology also showed characteristics consistent with this diagnosis.
The recurrence of the lesion, positive margins, and atypical keratinocytes suggest a malignant transformation of the initial hidradenoma.
The enlarged, firm right ala and tumor within the nasal vestibule floor and ala could be consistent with a cylindroma, a type of sweat gland tumor.
The downward papillomatous proliferation of keratinocytes and the location of the tumor in the nasal vestibule could suggest a syringocystadenoma papilliferum.
The positive margins and atypical keratinocytes, combined with the location of the tumor, could suggest a mucinous carcinoma.
The uncovered finding of p63 positive, pancytokeratin positive, and p16 negative pathology results explains the diagnosis of Hidradenoma papilliferum.
